Not much going on in the Marianas over the next few days. POPs 
(Probability of Precipitation) for the next week look to remain in
the 10 to 20 percent range. Enjoy the sunny days, but try to start
conserving water as we look to be moving into the dry season.

Marine/Surf...
The marine forecast remains relatively unchanged for the short term,
with combined seas of 4 to 6 feet tonight through Sunday night. Seas
then look to build a foot or so beginning Monday. As the seas
subsided, surf also fell below hazardous levels, so the High Surf
Advisory and the High Risk of Rip Currents were both cancelled a
little earlier this afternoon. The biggest change in the marine
forecast is the increase in the northwest swell that is expected to
move in from now Tropical Storm Cempaka (31W), expected to become a 
typhoon over the next 24 hours or so. This will push a modest 
northwest swell into the region by the middle of next week that looks
to become the dominant swell. With an expected long period, this 
could result in another high risk of rip currents and hazardous surf 
along west and north facing reefs.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm 31W is officially named Cempaka. At 1:00 PM ChST, 
Cempaka was located about 145 miles west-northwest of Agrihan near 
19.3N 143.5E, moving west-northwest at 18 mph. Maximum sustained 
winds have increased to 40 mph. Cempaka is expected to maintain its 
current heading with a decrease in forward speed over the next couple
of days, then turn toward the NNW around Tuesday. Cempaka is 
expected to strengthen over the next couple of days, possibly 
becoming a typhoon Sunday night. Cempaka no longer poses a threat to
any of the islands in the Marianas or Micronesia as it progresses.

For more information on TS Cempaka, see bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and by the 
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) is becoming more active with a 
broad circulation visible moving west and rotating slowly between 
Kosrae and Majuro. This will bring scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms to Pohnpei and Kosrae tonight through Monday night,
though coverage my briefly become isolated for Kosrae Sunday. Majuro
looks to remain fairly dry the whole forecast period with coverage
keeping steady as isolated. A slight chance of thunderstorms will be
possible tomorrow for Majuro, due to the close vicinity of the 
departing circulation. By mid-week, Kosrae and Pohnpei may also 
experience a couple days of dry weather before a new trough 
potentially moves into the region. 

Marine conditions are fairly benign though combined seas will
increase up to 7 feet tonight around Pohnpei due to a rising trade
wind swell. Otherwise, seas of 4 to 6 feet are expected across the
islands for most of the forecast period. Gentle winds tonight for 
Pohnpei and Majuro look to decrease slightly with light winds 
expected for much of the forecast for all islands. 

Western Micronesia...
Another period of isolated showers is expected tonight for Palau and
Yap. Then, an intensifying trough extending from a buffer 
circulation to the south will move through the areas Sunday through
Tuesday, drying out earlier for Yap by Monday night. A peak in 
rainfall is forecast for Sunday night, so numerous showers and 
isolated thunderstorms are expected with the possibility of locally 
heavy rainfall for both forecast areas. Gentle to moderate
northeasterlies will slightly decrease to light to gentle by Sunday
night, but heavier showers could produce gusts up to 20 kt. Current
model guidance indicates the trough exiting quickly, so isolated
showers and light to gentle northeasterlies could return around
mid-week.

A broad circulation sits well to the east-southeast near the 
Marshall Islands, but a trough extending from this circulation will 
increase shower activity south and near Chuuk after midnight. 
Isolated showers and gentle to moderate northeasterlies will continue
this evening, but scattered showers are forecast to move in after 
midnight, especially as nighttime instability increases during the 
overnight hours. Due to Chuuk being on the outer edge of this trough,
rainfall is not expected to continue beyond tonight, so isolated 
showers will return Sunday. Model guidance indicates the circulation 
moving westward over the next several days, so scattered showers 
could return to Chuuk Monday and Monday night as the circulation 
passes to the south. Winds will become light to gentle easterlies 
around this time, eventually decreasing to light and variable winds 
as the circulation drags a col over Chuuk. Drier conditions may 
return around mid-week.

Altimetry indicates combined seas of 3 to 5 ft across western
